chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from al-Hasan ibn Salih said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever performs ablution and does so well, then prays two rak'ahs, and completes their bowing and prostration, then sits and praises Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and sends blessings upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), then asks Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for his need, has indeed sought goodness in its sources. And whoever seeks goodness in its sources will not be disappointed.'

key_terms.صَلَّى عَلَى رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ: Sent blessings upon the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended method and prayer for fulfilling a specific need according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on the Prayer of the Need, this hadith establishes a precise spiritual protocol: after performing wudu with excellence and offering two rak'ahs with complete devotion, one concludes with praise (hamd) and blessings upon the Prophet (salawat) before supplicating. This sequence mirrors the prophetic tradition of using salawat as a means of intercession, ensuring that the petitioner seeks goodness in its proper channels ('mazanihi'), thereby guaranteeing the acceptance of their request without failure.
